title: Does the area rule still work for a trapezium that leans?
description: A trapezium leans to one side, so a line cannot simply drop straight down from each top corner. A line drawn from the top corner parallel to the slanting side cuts it into a parallelogram and a triangle, and the two areas are added. Keeko doubts this and takes the triangle as four times five, which is the whole rectangle round it.
teaching_notes: One idea: a line parallel to the slanting side cuts a leaning trapezium into a parallelogram and a triangle. Watch for students who forget that a triangle is half of the rectangle with the same base and height.

source: A slanting trapezium ABCD with parallel sides AB and DC, found as a parallelogram and a triangle
video_script.why: The child knows the areas of a parallelogram and a triangle, and here meets a trapezium with a leaning side, as the book does.
video_script.substitution: Numbers for the book's leaning trapezium: AB = 6 cm, DC = 10 cm and height 5 cm.
video_script.anchor: the leaning trapezium ABCD of the book with the line BG drawn parallel to AD
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes the triangle as base four times height five and says it is twenty square centimetres. That is the whole rectangle round the triangle, and the triangle fills only half of it.
video_script.payoff_line: The trapezium covers forty square centimetres.
maths_rules: trapezium ABCD: AB parallel to DC, AB = 6 cm, DC = 10 cm, height 5 cm
BG parallel to AD, G on DC: ABGD is a parallelogram, DG = AB = 6, area 6 x 5 = 30 cm2
GC = 10 - 6 = 4; triangle BGC: 1/2 x 4 x 5 = 10 cm2
Keeko: 4 x 5 = 20 is the rectangle round the triangle; the triangle is half of it, 10
video_script.design: One leaning trapezium stays all video. A line from the top corner parallel to the slanting side cuts it into a parallelogram and a triangle in two colours. The rule with half is written under the sum as a check. Keeko's rectangle is drawn round the triangle.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a trapezium that leans to one side.
<bookmark mark='lean'/>The top side eigh B is six centimetres and the bottom side D C is ten centimetres.
<bookmark mark='sides'/>The height between them is five centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many square centimetres does the trapezium cover?

beats.on_screen: the trapezium stays on the board and Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a line BG is drawn from B parallel to AD and meets DC at G; the parallelogram ABGD is shaded in one colour and the triangle BGC in a second colour

marks.draw: the line BG is drawn from B parallel to AD and meets DC at G
marks.para: the parallelogram ABGD is shaded and DG = AB is marked
marks.left: the triangle BGC is shaded in a second colour

beats.colours: parallelogram in one colour, triangle in a second colour
narration: <bookmark mark='draw'/>Draw a line from B parallel to eigh D, meeting D C at G.
<bookmark mark='para'/>Eigh B G D has both pairs of sides parallel, so it is a parallelogram. Opposite sides are equal, so D G is also six.
<bookmark mark='left'/>What is left is the triangle B G C.

beats.on_screen: Given: AB = 6 cm, DC = 10 cm, height 5 cm

marks.given: AB = 6 cm and DC = 10 cm are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the parallel sides are eigh B, six centimetres, and D C, ten centimetres.
<bookmark mark='height'/>The height between them is five centimetres.

beats.on_screen: To find: area of trapezium ABCD

marks.find: the words area of trapezium ABCD are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the area of the trapezium eigh B C D.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: parallelogram ABGD, area = base × height = 6 × 5 = 30 cm²

marks.para: the parallelogram ABGD lights up and the rule base × height is written

narration: <bookmark mark='para'/>Step one, find the parallelogram. Its area is base times height, six times five.
<bookmark mark='val'/>That gives thirty square centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: GC = 10 - 6 = 4; triangle BGC, area = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 4 × 5 = 10 cm²

marks.gc: GC = 10 - 6 = 4 is written on the base of the triangle
marks.tri: the rule 1/2 × base × height is written with the values 4 and 5

narration: <bookmark mark='gc'/>Step two, find the triangle. G C is ten take away six, so it is four centimetres.
<bookmark mark='tri'/>Area of a triangle is half times base times height, so half times four times five.
<bookmark mark='val'/>That gives ten square centimetres.

marks.add: the two shaded pieces slide together and the words parallelogram + triangle are written

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the two areas, because the trapezium is made of both pieces.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Thirty plus ten.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check with the rule, area = 1/2 × height × (sum of parallel sides) = 1/2 × 5 × (6 + 10)

marks.rule: the rule 1/2 × height × (sum of parallel sides) is written
marks.vals: the values 5, 6 and 10 replace the words

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step four, check with the rule from your book. Area is half times height times the sum of the parallel sides.
<bookmark mark='vals'/>Half times five times six plus ten.

beats.on_screen: Answer: area of trapezium ABCD = 40 cm², both ways

marks.both: the two working lines are joined by an equals sign

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The trapezium covers forty square centimetres.
<bookmark mark='both'/>Adding the pieces and using the rule give the same area, even though the side leans.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the triangle is four times five, which is twenty square centimetres.
<bookmark mark='box'/>But four by five is the whole rectangle drawn round the triangle.
<bookmark mark='half'/>The triangle fills only half of that rectangle.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Half of twenty is ten, so the triangle is ten square centimetres, as we found.
